title: Add Iris $15 lifetime budget guard and record it for OLY-B-SET-04
summary: Build a small Rust module in athena-core that reads a committed Iris spend ledger and refuses any generation that would push lifetime spend over $15, then record it as OLY-B-SET-04's mechanism and measure in docs/spec.toml. Audience: Athena's owner and the verifier checking the spec gap list clears.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require new passing unit tests plus fmt, clippy and test.
Criteria run the budget guard on over, at and under budget cases.
Ledger holds only amounts; test checks no credential fields.
One module, one ledger file, one spec entry.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (spec gap sweep: blank_or_none mechanism check, measure label validation, steward request text ~lines 1163-1350) and crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (~line 302 and 506, status labels). A grep for iris/ledger under crates/ found nothing, so no Iris code exists yet; BRIEF.md lines 28 and 361 say assets come from Iris within $15, tracked in a committed ledger and checked before every generation, credentials never in the repo.
Existing code: extend docs/spec.toml (OLY-B-SET-04 entry currently mechanism = "none") and follow the style of crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs; no existing Iris code to reuse.

Design: a new module crates/athena-core/src/iris.rs with a pure function that takes ledger entries (amount in cents) and a proposed cost and returns Ok or a refusal when the lifetime total would exceed 1500 cents. Ledger is a committed TOML file at docs/iris-ledger.toml, starting with zero entries. It holds no credentials. Integer cents avoid float error.

The 'harness-engineering bundle as a reference' half is met by a documented reference in the ledger/module docs or docs/ and is prose-only; the mechanism enforced is the budget. The measure states this.

Measure: the measure ends with 'status: not shown' and names the test, e.g. 'cargo test -p athena-core iris; status: not shown', unless an existing `athena status` label fits directly. Producer should check the labels at status.rs ~302 and choose.

The new ledger file is parsed from docs/, not a record file under crates/, so check_record_file/AnyRecord are not touched; if the producer adds a data file under crates/, it must be covered by check_record_file and the AnyRecord round-trip test.
Not a new refusal on past readings: the rule gates Iris generation only, which has no past use, so expected 0% of newly refused readings.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/spec.toml entry OLY-B-SET-04 has a mechanism naming crates/athena-core/src/iris.rs and docs/iris-ledger.toml (not "none"), keeps owner = "Athena", and has a measure ending in 'status: not shown' or an `athena status` label, naming the test. Verify with Grep on docs/spec.toml and that the named files exist.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core iris`: a test shows a generation costing enough to exceed 1500 cents lifetime is refused, one within budget is allowed, and exactly 1500 cents is allowed. The refusal tests fail if the guard is removed or made to always allow.
A test reads the committed docs/iris-ledger.toml and shows it parses, the total is at most 1500 cents, and it contains no credential-like fields; run with cargo test -p athena-core iris.
A hestia spec-gap test (cargo test -p athena-core hestia) or equivalent shows OLY-B-SET-04 no longer appears in the spec gap list with no mechanism or bad measure.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy (workspace, all targets) and cargo test all pass.
CHANGELOG.md gains an entry for the Iris budget guard; no files outside the deliverables, no secrets, and records/ untouched.

out_of_scope: Calling the real Iris service or handling Iris credentials
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows or other governance files
hard_reason: It adds a rule that can refuse work (a spend gate that refuses Iris generation over budget).
